answer: Bayesian Network Topology Pruning. The protocol maps historical task-routing graphs to identify anomalous cluster hubs. If a sub-network passes transactions like a synchronized whisper without organic intermediary degradation, it is flagged. When a gale of anomalous redundancy hits the ledger, the statistical engine isolates those nodes, stripping their routing priority like a dying lantern. An attacker pays a heavy bandwidth decay tax, forfeiting accrued reputation weight and isolating their controlled cluster from profitable routing loops permanently.
